A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MCMARK research. Text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–D support reliable comparison after matching relocated material and renumbered tables.

before.justification: Sections 5 and Appendix D report original watermark detection, token-replacement robustness, translation and summarization quality experiments, and distribution-channel ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds robustness results under GPT rephrasing, GPT back-translation and DIPPER attacks in Tables 3–5.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Algorithms 1–4 retain the same vocabulary partitioning, distribution-channel reweighting, watermark-key-based sampling and detection procedures. The new attacks evaluate the existing method.

E1.justification: Section 5.3 expands robustness coverage from token replacement to GPT rephrasing, GPT back-translation and DIPPER. These introduce substantially different text-transformation conditions. The underlying datasets and generation, translation and summarization tasks are retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in corresponding experiments. The new attack tables reuse ITS-edit, EXP-edit, γ-reweight, DiPmark at α=0.3 and 0.4, and STA-1. DIPPER is an attack, not a new watermark baseline.

E3.justification: The new robustness tables report AUC and TPR at FPRs of 5%, 1%, 0.1% and 0.01%, extending the original robustness table's metrics. Retained experimental settings are unchanged; detailed configurations for the new attacks are not specified.

E4.justification: Tables 3–5 add substantial evidence about watermark survival under paraphrasing and back-translation, beyond v1's token-replacement tests. Existing channel-count ablations and detectability–robustness analyses in Figures 5–6 and 8–11 remain unchanged.

E5.justification: No repeated-run information, seeds, confidence intervals or uncertainty-estimation procedures are added. The new tables provide point estimates and median detection p-values without introducing a new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 3–5 newly report MCMARK TPRs at 0.1% FPR of 31.7% under GPT rephrasing, 86.8% under GPT back-translation and 3.6% under DIPPER. Under DIPPER, EXP-edit reaches 3.5%. These are new attack results, not same-setting performance changes. Existing tables and figures retain their results.

T1.justification: The distribution-channel definitions, optimization and solution in Equations 1–3, binomial detection calculation, expected true-negative-rate analysis and Appendix B derivation are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the claims of unbiasedness, model-agnostic detection, a two-channel theoretical advantage, improved robustness and over 10% better detectability. The additional experiments do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: The mechanism explanations, channel-count trade-off and stated limitation remain substantively unchanged. V2 adds no specific interpretation or qualification addressing the weak detection under DIPPER.

D1.justification: The abstract adds a code-availability statement and repository address. Appendix C retains its model, sample-count, watermark-key and hyperparameter information. The new attacks receive no detailed implementation settings.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations concerning De-mark, watermarked protein design, ZeroMark, watermark-key collisions and DIPPER paraphrasing. The related-work discussion and novelty positioning remain largely unchanged. The expanded MBART reference identifies the same previously cited work.

P1.justification: Edits include the code statement, brief additions to the robustness description, expanded author contact information and acknowledgments. Almost all prose and the section and appendix organization are retained.

P2.justification: Three full-width robustness tables are added, and Figures 5–6 change from a vertical stack to a side-by-side arrangement. Existing figures are retained; appendix Tables 3–4 become Tables 6–7 with small formatting adjustments.

improvement.justification: V2 improves the empirical assessment by adding paraphrasing and back-translation tests beyond v1's token replacements, and supplies a code address. The gains are limited by unspecified attack configurations and unchanged discussion that does not acknowledge MCMARK's 3.6% TPR at 0.1% FPR under DIPPER. The added evidence is useful, but its reproducibility and interpretation remain incomplete.
